paragraphs: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. ("Parent") is a New Jersey insurance holding company incorporated in 1977. It owns ten property and casualty insurance subsidiaries ("Insurance Subsidiaries") that sell products and services only in the United States ("U.S.") and exclusively through independent insurance agents and wholesale brokers. Nine of our Insurance Subsidiaries are licensed by various state insurance departments as admitted carriers, allowing them to write specific property and casualty lines in the standard market. The tenth subsidiary is authorized as a non-admitted carrier to write property and casualty insurance in the excess and surplus ("E&S") lines market. Throughout this document, we refer to the Parent and the Insurance Subsidiaries collectively as "we," "us," or "our." We use "Parent" when appropriate to distinguish it from the Insurance Subsidiaries. Specific terms related to the property and casualty industry are defined in a glossary attached as Exhibit 99.1 to this Form 10-K.

We have a long and successful history in the property and casualty insurance industry dating back to our 1926 founding. We list our common (stock symbol "SIGI") and preferred (stock symbol "SIGIP") stocks on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. In 2025, AM Best Company ("AM Best") ranked us as the 34th largest property and casualty group in its annual "Top 200 U.S. Property/Casualty Writers" list based on 2024 net premiums written ("NPW"). Our current AM Best financial strength rating is "A+" (Superior).

Our competitive and crowded market requires us to clearly articulate and demonstrate our value proposition to customers, distribution partners, employees, and investors. We believe our five key sustainable competitive advantages are:
•A unique operating model that places empowered decision-makers alongside our customers and distribution partners.
•A franchise-value distribution model, characterized by close and meaningful business relationships with a select group of high-quality distribution partners.
•An ability to develop and integrate sophisticated technology tools that support our front-line employees in making informed risk selection, pricing, and claims decisions.
•A commitment to delivering a superior omnichannel customer experience, enhanced by people and technology.
•A highly engaged and aligned team of extremely talented employees.

Several nationally recognized statistical rating organizations ("NRSROs") evaluate and rate our financial strength, operating performance, strategic position, and ability to meet policyholder obligations.
AM Best A+ Stable Standard & Poor's Global Ratings ("S&P") A Stable Moody's Investors Services ("Moody's") A2 Stable

We believe our AM Best rating most significantly influences our ability to write insurance business. Our independent distribution partners recommend insurance carriers based partly on financial strength ratings to (i) ensure an insurance carrier's ability to pay claims and provide benefits to customers when needed, directly impacting the level of trust a customer has in an insurance carrier and (ii) limit their potential liability for customer error and omission claims. Similarly, many customers consider ratings when purchasing insurance because their loan, mortgage, and other real and personal property security agreements typically require minimum carrier financial strength rating requirements.

These NRSROs also evaluate and rate our long-term debt creditworthiness and capacity to meet obligations when they come due. Credit ratings significantly influence our overall funding profile and ability to access certain types of liquidity. Our current senior debt credit ratings are as follows:
AM Best a- Stable S&P BBB Stable Moody's Baa2 Stable Fitch BBB+ Stable
Our S&P, Moody's, and Fitch financial strength and credit ratings influence our ability to advantageously access capital markets more than our AM Best rating.

headings: Risks Related to our Insurance Operations
We are subject to losses from catastrophic events.
Our loss and loss expense reserves may not adequately cover actual losses and expenses.
Our ability to reduce our risk exposure depends on the availability and cost of reinsurance.
We are exposed to credit risk.
National and global economic conditions could adversely and materially affect our business, results of operations, financial condition, and growth.

A downgrade or a potential downgrade in our financial strength or credit ratings could result in a loss of business and have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Markets for insurance products and services are highly competitive and subject to rapid technological advancement, and we may struggle to compete effectively.
We have less loss experience data than our larger competitors.
We are subject to various modeling risks that could have a material adverse impact on our business results.
Risks Related to Our Investments Segment
Our investments are exposed to credit risk, interest rate fluctuation, and changes in value.
We are subject to the risks inherent in investing in private limited partnerships.
Determining the amount of credit losses taken on our investments is highly subjective and could materially impact our results of operations or our financial position.
Risks Related to Evolving Laws, Regulations, and Public Policy Debates
Our business is subject to various state, federal, and other laws, rules, policies, and other data use and protection obligations.
Risks Related to Our Corporate Structure and Governance

We are a holding company, and our ability to declare dividends to our shareholders, pay indebtedness, and enter into affiliate transactions may be limited because our Insurance Subsidiaries are regulated.
Because we are a New Jersey corporation and an insurance holding company, we may be less attractive to potential acquirers, and our common stock's value could be adversely affected.
Risks Related to Our General Operations
We, our distribution partners, and vendors are subject to attempted cyber-attacks and other cybersecurity and system availability risks.
Operational leverage relies on the success of our risk management strategies, and their failure could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.
paragraphs: Certain risk factors can significantly impact our business, liquidity, capital resources, results of operations, financial condition, and debt ratings. These risk factors might affect, alter, or change actions we take to execute our long-term capital strategy. Examples include, without limitation, contributing capital to any or all of our ten property and casualty insurance subsidiaries ("Insurance Subsidiaries"), issuing additional debt and/or equity securities, repurchasing our existing debt and/or equity securities, or increasing or decreasing common stockholders' dividends. We operate in a continually changing business environment, and new risk factors that we cannot predict or assess may emerge at any time. Consequently, we cannot predict these new risk factors or assess their potential future impact on our business.

Losses from natural and human-made catastrophes can negatively impact our financial results. Examples include hurricanes, tornadoes, windstorms, earthquakes, hail, thunderstorms, severe winter weather, derechos, floods, and fires, some of which are related to climate change, as well as criminal and terrorist acts, including cyber-attacks, civil unrest, and explosions. The frequency and severity of these catastrophes are inherently unpredictable, and both have increased globally in recent years. In many cases, the increase in catastrophe losses relates to small- to- medium-sized events that primary insurers retain rather than cede to reinsurers. We use sophisticated catastrophe modeling techniques to manage our exposure, but actual exposure and loss experience can materially differ from catastrophe model estimates. For example, catastrophe models did not fully estimate the potential for some recent catastrophe losses (such as Winter Storm Elliott freeze losses in December 2022) and the concurrent economic inflation on construction costs.

Our most significant natural and/or human-made catastrophe exposures are (i) hurricanes impacting the Eastern U.S., (ii) severe convective storms, including hailstorms and tornadoes, (iii) winter storms, (iv) wildfires, (v) earthquakes, and (vi) terrorism events. Single storms could adversely impact our financial results; however, we could experience more than one severe catastrophic event in any given calendar year. We track our severe weather and catastrophe losses using definitions and information from Insurance Services Office, Inc.'s ("ISO") Property Claim Services unit, an internationally recognized authority on insured property losses from catastrophes in the U.S., Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
Certain factors can impact our estimates of ultimate costs for natural and/or human-made catastrophes, including:
•Inability to access portions of the affected areas after a catastrophic event;
•Scarcity of necessary labor and materials that delay repairs and increase our loss costs;

paragraphs: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. ("Parent") 為一間新澤西州保險控股公司，於1977年成立。本公司擁有十間財產與意外保險子公司 ("Insurance Subsidiaries")，僅在美國 ("U.S.") 銷售產品與服務，並 exclusively 透過獨立保險經紀與批發經紀進行銷售。九間 Insurance Subsidiaries 已經獲各州保險部門許可為 admitted carriers，使其能在標準市場提供特定財產與意外保險業務。第十間子公司則被授權為 non-admitted carrier，可在過失與餘額 ("E&S") 市場提供財產與意外保險。於本文件中，我們將 Parent 與 Insurance Subsidiaries 合稱為 "we," "us," 或 "our." 我們會使用 "Parent" 來區分 Insurance Subsidiaries。與財產與意外保險產業相關的特定術語，已於本 Form 10-K 附屬的 Exhibit 99.1 附錄中定義。

我們在財產與意外保險產業擁有悠久且成功的歷史，可追溯至1926年成立。我們的普通股 (股票代碼 "SIGI") 與優先股 (股票代碼 "SIGIP") 登記於 Nasdaq Global Select Market。2025年，AM Best Company ("AM Best") 將我們列為年度 "Top 200 U.S. Property/Casualty Writers" 名單中第34大的財產與意外保險集團，根據2024年淨保費收入 ("NPW") 來計算。我們目前的 AM Best 財務強度評級為 "A+" (Superior)。
我們所處的競爭激烈市場，要求我們明確說明並展示對客戶、分銷夥伴、員工與投資人的價值主張。我們相信我們的五大可持續競爭優勢為：
• 一種獨特的營運模式，將賦權的決策者與客戶及分銷夥伴並肩作戰。
• 一種特許價值的分銷模式，特徵為與少數高品質分銷夥伴建立密切且有意義的商業關係。
• 能夠開發並整合先進的科技工具，以支援前線員工做出明智的風險選擇、定價與理賠決策。
• 堅持提供優越的全渠道客戶體驗，並透過人力與科技加以提升。
• 一個高度投入且一致的極具才能員工團隊。
數家 nationally recognized statistical rating organizations ("NRSROs") 評估並評定我們的財務強度、營運表現、戰略地位以及履行保單責任的能力。
AM Best A+ 穩定 Standard & Poor's Global Ratings ("S&P") A 穩定 Moody's Investors Services ("Moody's") A2 穩定

我們認為 AM Best 評級最顯著影響我們寫單保險業務的能力。我們的獨立通路夥伴在推薦保險電信業者時，部分根據財務強度評級，以 (i) 確保保險電信業者在需要時能支付賠款並提供客戶利益，直接影響客戶對保險電信業者的信任程度，以及 (ii) 限制其因客戶過失與遺漏申訴而可能產生的潛在責任。同樣地，許多客戶在購買保險時會考慮評級，因為他們的貸款、房貸及其他實質與個人財產擔保協議通常會要求最低的電信業者財務強度評級要求。
這些 NRSROs 也會評估並評定我們長期債務的信用worthiness 以及履行義務的能力。信用評級顯著影響我們整體的資金結構以及取得特定類型流動性的能力。我們目前的高階債務信用評級如下：
AM Best a- 穩定 S&P BBB 穩定 Moody's Baa2 穩定 Fitch BBB+ 穩定
我們的 S&P、Moody's 與 Fitch 財務強度與信用評級，比 AM Best 評級更顯著影響我們以優勢條件進入資本市場的能力。

我們透過九家保險子公司銷售標準商業保險與標準個人保險產品及服務，其中一些參與聯邦政府國家洪水保險計劃（"NFIP"）的 Write Your Own 程式（"WYO"）。我們透過另一家子公司 Mesa Underwriters Specialty Insurance Company（"MUSIC"），一家全國性授權但非承認的平台，為一般無法在標準市場取得保障的客戶提供 E&S 產品。
我們 collectively 會稱這十家保險子公司為「保險子公司」。

以下為管理層對我們財務狀況及合併營運成果的討論與分析（"MD&A"），包括對營運及外部來源現金流數量與確定性的評估，以及可能對未來期間有重大影響的趨勢與不確定性。MD&A 討論並分析我們 2025 年的結果與 2024 年的比較。投資人應配合本 Form 10-K 第 8 項「財務報表及補充資料」閱讀 MD&A。如需討論與分析我們 2024 年結果與 2023 年的比較，請參閱我們 2024 年財務年度（截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日）年度報告 Form 10-K 中第 7 項「財務狀況與營運成果的管理層討論與分析」。
在管理討論與分析（MD&A）中，我們將討論並分析以下項目：•關鍵會計政策與會計估計；
•2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日的財務亮點與結果；•各應報告分部的營運結果及相關資訊；
我們已識別出對我們營運及瞭解我們營運結果至關重要的政策與估計。我們認為對財務報表編製至關重要的政策與估計為（i）損失與損失費用備抵，（ii）投資評價及應計信用減損允許額於可供出售（"AFS"）固定收入證券，以及（iii）再保險；
從保險事故發生、向我們報案，至最終賠償與付款，可能需要經過相當長的時間。保險公司會建立備抵作為資產負債表負債，以確認未償付損失與損失費用的負債。以下表格提供截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的損失與損失費用備抵（包括已發生但未報案（"IBNR"）備抵）及未償付損失與損失費用的再保險賠償；

headings: 與我們保險業務相關的風險
我們可能因重大災難事件而遭受損失。
我們的損失及損失費用備抵可能無法充分覆蓋實際的損失及費用。
我們降低風險敞口的能力取決於再保險的可得性及成本。
國家及全球經濟情勢可能對我們的業務、營運成果、財務狀況及成長產生不利且重大的影響。
我們的財務健全等級或信用評級若遭降級或有降級風險，可能會導致業務流失，並對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
保險產品及服務市場競爭激烈，且技術進步迅速，本公司可能難以有效競爭。
本公司較大型競爭對手擁有較少的損失經驗資料。
本公司面臨各種模型風險，這些風險可能對本公司營運成果產生重大不利影響。
與投資業務相關的風險
本公司投資面臨信用風險、利率波動及價值變動的風險。
本公司投資於私人有限合夥企業，會面臨內在風險。
本公司投資所產生的信用損失金額，其評估具有高度主觀性，可能對本公司營運成果或財務狀況產生重大影響。
與不斷演進的法律、法規及公共政策辯論相關的風險
本公司業務受各州、聯邦及其他法律、規則、政策及其他資料使用與保護義務所規範。
與本公司企業結構及治理相關之風險
本公司為控股公司，因我們的保險子公司受監管，故本公司對股東宣告紅利、償還債務及進行關聯交易之能力可能受到限制。
因本公司為紐約州公司且為保險控股公司，可能較不具吸引力於潛在收購者，且本公司普通股之價值可能受到不利影響。
與本公司一般營運相關之風險
本公司、我們的經銷夥伴及供應商可能面臨網路攻擊及其他資安與系統可用性風險之威脅。
營運槓桿依賴我們風險管理策略之成功，其失敗可能對本公司財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 某些風險因素可能顯著影響我們的業務、流動性、資本資源、營運結果、財務狀況及債務評級。這些風險因素可能影響、改變或改變我們執行長期資本策略的行動。範例包括，但不限於，向任何或全部我們的十家財產與意外保險子公司（"保險子公司"）注資、發行額外的債務及/或權益證券、回購我們現有的債務及/或權益證券，或提高或降低普通股股東的股息。我們營運於持續變化的商業環境中，且我們無法預測或評估的新的風險因素可能隨時出現。因此，我們無法預測這些新的風險因素或評估它們對我們業務的潛在未來影響。

自然及人為災難造成的損失可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。範例包括颶風、龍捲風、風暴、地震、冰雹、雷暴、嚴寒天氣、derechos、洪水及火災，其中一些與氣候變遷有關，以及刑事犯罪及恐怖攻擊，包括網路攻擊、社會動亂及爆炸。這些災難的發生頻率及嚴重程度本質上是無法預測的，且近年來在全球範圍內均有增加。在許多情況下，災難損失的增加與小至中型事件有關，而這些事件主要由直接保險公司承擔，而非轉嫁給再保險公司。我們使用先進的災難模型技術來管理我們的風險敞口，但實際的風險敞口及損失經驗可能與災難模型預估有顯著差異。例如，災難模型未能充分預估某些近期災難損失（如2022年12月Winter Storm Elliott凍結損失）以及同時發生的建設成本經濟膨脹。

我們最重大的自然及/或人為災難風險敞口為（i）影響美國東部的颶風、（ii）嚴重對流性天氣，包括冰雹及龍捲風、（iii）冬季風暴、（iv）野火、（v）地震，以及（vi）恐怖攻擊事件。單一風暴可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響；然而，我們可能在任何一個財曆年內經歷多於一次嚴重的災難事件。我們使用保險服務辦公室（Insurance Services Office, Inc.）（"ISO"）財產聲請服務部門（Property Claim Services unit）所提供的定義及資訊來追蹤我們的嚴重天氣及災難損失，該部門是美國、波多黎各及美國維京羣島地區 insured 財產損失的國際知名權威機構。
某些因素可能影響我們對自然及/或人於災難最終成本的預估，包括：
•在災難事件後無法進入受影響區域的部分地區；
•必要勞動力及材料的短缺會延誤修復工作並增加我們的損失成本；
